record.question: They say that the banker is on his last legs
record.explanation: Answer A: the verge of ruin. “On one’s last legs” means near the end/close to collapse; “the verge of ruin” is closest among these choices. Independent check: “On his last legs” describes being near collapse/end; “the verge of ruin” is closest in this context. Reference: https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/idiom. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Exact printed question, choices and required directions/emphasis reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.
